exercicio.statement:
Katie and Franklin each brought a piece of cheese to the school picnic. Katie and Franklin brought different types of cheese so it looks like they brought the same amount, but not necessarily the same weight. Katie claims that her cheese is heavier. Is this true?
Katie's cheese weighs 2/5 of a pound.
Franklin's cheese weighs 2/3 of a pound.
Is Katie right?

Set Katie's number line to show the denominator of her fraction.
nodes.instruction: Set Katie's number line to show the denominator of her fraction.

hints.message: Which number tells how many equal parts make the whole?
Look at the bottom number of Katie's fraction and use it for the number of equal parts.
Katie's fraction is 2/5. The denominator is the number 5.
Type the denominator from 2/5 into the field, then confirm the division of the number line.

misconceptions.description: O aluno confunde o papel do numerador e denominador ao preparar a reta.
misconceptions.feedback: You used the numerator as the number of divisions. In 2/5, the denominator 5 tells how many equal parts make the whole.

misconceptions.description: O aluno conta as marcas (traços) que delimitam as partes, resultando em um intervalo a mais.
misconceptions.feedback: You counted the boundary marks instead of the spaces between them. Five equal parts require a denominator of 5.

nodes.description: Mark Katie's fraction on her number line.
nodes.instruction: Mark Katie's fraction on her number line.

hints.message: What does the numerator tell you to count on the divided number line?
Starting at 0, count equal intervals toward 1 using the numerator.
Katie's line has five equal intervals, and her numerator is 2.
Click the second division mark after 0 on Katie's number line.

nodes.description: Set Franklin's number line to show the denominator of his fraction.
nodes.instruction: Set Franklin's number line to show the denominator of his fraction.

hints.message: Which part of a fraction tells the number of equal sections in the whole?
Use the bottom number of Franklin's fraction as the number of equal parts.
Franklin's fraction is 2/3. Its denominator is 3.
Type 3 into Franklin's denominator field and confirm the three equal parts.

misconceptions.description: O aluno confunde o papel do numerador e denominador ao preparar a reta.
misconceptions.feedback: You used the numerator as the number of divisions. In 2/3, the denominator 3 tells how many equal parts make the whole.

misconceptions.description: O aluno conta as marcas (traços) que delimitam as partes, resultando em um intervalo a mais.
misconceptions.feedback: You counted the boundary marks instead of the spaces between them. Three equal parts require a denominator of 3.

nodes.description: Mark Franklin's fraction on his number line.
nodes.instruction: Mark Franklin's fraction on his number line.

hints.message: How many equal intervals from 0 does Franklin's numerator ask you to move?
Use the numerator to count intervals on Franklin's number line.
Franklin's line has three equal intervals, and his numerator is 2.
Click the second division mark after 0 on Franklin's number line.

nodes.description: Use the two marked points to compare the cheese weights.
nodes.instruction: Use the two marked points to compare the cheese weights.

expectedInput.value: No. Katie is not right. The piece of cheese Franklin brought is heavier.
acceptableVariations: No. Katie is not right. The piece of cheese Franklin brought is heavier.

options.value: Yes; the piece of cheese Katie brought is heavier.
options.label: Yes; the piece of cheese Katie brought is heavier.
options.feedback: You treated the larger denominator as if it made the fraction larger. With the same numerator, dividing the whole into more parts makes each part smaller, so 2/5 is less than 2/3.

options.value: No. Katie is not right. The piece of cheese Franklin brought is heavier.
options.label: No. Katie is not right. The piece of cheese Franklin brought is heavier.

options.value: Both pieces of cheese weigh the same.
options.label: Both pieces of cheese weigh the same.
options.feedback: You compared the differences between the numerator and denominator instead of the fraction values. Use the positions on the number lines to compare the actual amounts.

hints.message: On number lines from 0 to 1, which point farther to the right represents the greater amount?
Compare the positions of the two marked points rather than comparing only their denominators.
Both fractions have numerator 2, so examine how far two parts reach on each number line.
Choose the statement saying that Franklin's piece is heavier, then continue to the final confirmation.

misconceptions.description: O aluno acredita que quanto maior o denominador, maior a fração, ignorando a partição do inteiro.
misconceptions.feedback: Check the number lines again. A larger denominator means the whole is split into more, smaller parts; therefore 2/5 is not greater than 2/3.
